h1: Buri Sriphu Hotel — a 4-star boutique in Greenway within walking distance of Hat Yai's ASEAN Night Bazaar
intro: If your main reason for visiting Hat Yai is the ASEAN Night Bazaar, the street food and shopping at Central Festival, Buri Sriphu Hotel sits right in the middle of it all — a 4-star boutique hotel in the Greenway district. Opened in 2012, it earns steady praise for clean rooms, comfortable beds and an outdoor saltwater pool that's bigger than most city hotels manage. There are 136 rooms, a kids' pool, gym, spa and an on-site convention centre. Rates start from approximately THB 1,500/night, and it holds a 9.0 score from 426 reviews on Trip.com — the draw is the nightlife-district location plus a pool and free parking you won't find right on the busiest streets.

body.html: What keeps Buri Sriphu Hotel in the conversation is its location in the Greenway district, near the ASEAN Night Bazaar — one of the night-eating and shopping spots people actually come to Hat Yai for. The bazaar is a short walk away, and Central Festival Hat Yai with its mall, restaurants and cinema is close by. It's the kind of spot that suits travellers who want to head out for street food in the evening and stroll back to the hotel without calling a ride every time.

The hotel opened in 2012 and has 136 rooms, ranging from Standard and Superior up to a Honeymoon Suite. Many reviews praise the rooms as spacious and clean with comfortable beds, and a good number of bathrooms come with a bathtub — not something you often get at this price. Every room has a fridge, TV and free Wi-Fi, and the decor leans warm and boutique rather than corporate tower.

"Very clean room, comfortable bed and even a bathtub. The pool is big and the water was clear, and it's just a few minutes' walk to the night bazaar. Staff were helpful and breakfast had a decent spread."

The shared facilities are well rounded for a city hotel. The outdoor saltwater pool with a kids' pool and poolside bar comes up often in reviews as bigger and clearer than expected, making it a good pick for families with children. There's a gym, a spa tub, an on-site restaurant and cafe, and a convention centre that hosts seminars and weddings. Free parking and an EV charging station are a real plus for anyone driving in from elsewhere in the province or up from Malaysia.

Service scores consistently well. Plenty of reviews highlight friendly, helpful staff — booking taxis, recommending places to eat and arranging tours. Breakfast offers both Thai and international options and is widely seen as solid value at this price, though some guests wish for more variety on busier mornings.

The honest caveat is that room quality isn't uniform across the property. A few reviews mention a musty smell or signs of damp in certain rooms, and noisy air-conditioning on some nights. Because the hotel has a convention centre and hosts weddings, you may occasionally hear noise from functions. The pool and gym have also closed temporarily for maintenance in past stretches, so if you're coming specifically to swim, confirm with the hotel before booking.

Rates start around THB 1,500/night for a Standard room in normal periods, with Superior rooms running roughly THB 1,700–2,200 and the Honeymoon Suite from about THB 3,000 depending on the dates. During long weekends and festivals, when Malaysian and Singaporean visitors pour into Hat Yai, prices climb and rooms fill fast. The 9.0 score from 426 Trip.com reviews reflects a city hotel that guests are happy with overall, especially on cleanliness and location.

In short, Buri Sriphu Hotel suits travellers here for the night bazaar, the food and the shopping, families who want a pool for the kids, and drivers who need easy parking. If the Greenway location, the pool and a rate in the low thousands of baht are what you're after, it fits well. But if you want a hotel connected directly to a mall, or rooms that are uniformly polished, it's worth comparing against other central options first.

A tip drawn from the reviews: ask for a recently renovated or higher-floor room to avoid musty smells and noise. If you're travelling with kids, request a room near the pool. Check with the hotel whether your dates clash with a wedding or seminar if you want quiet, and book a Free Cancellation rate where you can — especially over long weekends when rooms sell out quickly.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Buri Sriphu Hotel Hat Yai

faq.q: Where is Buri Sriphu Hotel and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's at 310 Sripoovanart Road in the Greenway district of central Hat Yai, Songkhla Province. It's about a 5-minute walk to the ASEAN Night Bazaar, roughly 5–7 minutes' drive to Central Festival Hat Yai and Kim Yong Market, around 7 minutes from Hat Yai Railway Station and about 20 minutes' drive from Hat Yai Airport (HDY).

faq.q: How much does Buri Sriphu Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approximately THB 1,500/night for a Standard room. Superior rooms run about THB 1,700–2,200, there's a Superior Twin for two single beds, and the Honeymoon Suite is from around THB 3,000. Prices depend on the dates and climb fast over long weekends, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Buri Sriphu Hotel really near ASEAN Night Bazaar?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel sits in the Greenway district, about a 5-minute walk from the ASEAN Night Bazaar, Hat Yai's night-time eating and shopping hub. It suits travellers who want to head out for street food in the evening and walk back to the hotel without calling a ride each time.

faq.q: Who is Buri Sriphu Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a good fit for travellers here for the night bazaar, food and shopping, families who want a pool for the kids, and drivers who need easy parking. Its strengths are the Greenway location and the pool. It's less ideal if you want a hotel connected to a mall or need especially quiet surroundings.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Buri Sriphu Hotel?
faq.a: Room quality isn't uniform. Some reviews mention a musty smell, damp or noisy air-conditioning in certain rooms, so ask for a recently renovated or higher-floor room. The hotel has a convention centre and hosts weddings, so functions can be noisy at times. The pool and gym have closed for maintenance in past periods, so check first if you're coming to swim.

faq.q: Does Buri Sriphu Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes. There's an outdoor saltwater pool with a kids' pool and poolside bar that reviewers describe as big and clear, plus a gym, spa, restaurant and cafe. Breakfast offers both Thai and international options and is widely seen as good value at this price, though choices can thin out on busy mornings.
